definitions.canonical_word: the output of encode_formula, which starts with MAGIC=11100101
definitions.row_projection: Rows(U_n)={r: there exists c with complement_contains(n,r,c)=True}

proof_steps.derivation: At level 3, side=8 and half=4. The frozen complement_contains definition can return true only in the old-old branch row<4,column<4 or the old-new branch row<4<=column; every remaining quadrant returns false. Therefore every supported row r satisfies 0<=r<4=2^(3-1), so Rows(U_3) is contained in [0,4).

Fix k>=3 and assume Rows(U_k) is contained in [0,2^(k-1)). At level k+1, side=2^(k+1) and half=2^k. A true complement_contains call is either old-old, where the row label is inherited and in particular r<2^k, or old-new, whose branch guard explicitly requires r<2^k. The other two quadrants return false. Thus Rows(U_(k+1)) is contained in [0,2^k)=[0,2^((k+1)-1)). By induction from P1 this holds for every n>=3, hence for every n>=17.

Every canonical word output by encode_formula starts with MAGIC=11100101, so its first bit is 1. For n>=17, its n-bit prefix therefore has binary value at least 2^(n-1), and every n-bit value is below 2^n. Hence every such prefix lies in [2^(n-1),2^n).

For fixed n>=17, P2 places Rows(U_n) in LOW_n=[0,2^(n-1)), while P3 places each canonical n-bit prefix in HIGH_n=[2^(n-1),2^n). LOW_n and HIGH_n are disjoint by their endpoints. Therefore no canonical UNSAT prefix row, a subset of the canonical prefix set, can collide with Rows(U_n) at any n>=17 in the frozen one-sided family.

statement_checked: For every n >= 17, Rows(U_n) is contained in [0,2^(n-1)) while every n-bit prefix of a canonical length-2n MAGIC word is in [2^(n-1),2^n); hence the projections are disjoint.
